assessment.best_option_considered: int_bundle (Bundle offer at 8% off co-bought SKUs, adding Rs. 369 to basket value)
assessment.expected_value_reasoning: int_bundle was the strongest option because it actively counteracted the two-month decline in AOV by increasing basket size. However, even int_bundle requires a +2.00 percentage point absolute conversion lift (to 20.60%) to break even on net contribution. Given that 42% of traffic is New Arrivals who care primarily about delivery reliability and sizing clarity (not price), and 22% are Gift Buyers who care about delivery dates over price, the probability of achieving a +2.00% conversion lift from a bundle offer is far too low to justify spending the merchant's single remaining experiment.

assessment.prediction: Waiving the Rs.30 shipping fee will increase overall conversion rate from 19.0% to 22.5% (+3.5 percentage points absolute), resulting in positive net incremental contribution per customer after accounting for the Rs.30 cost line.
assessment.reasoning: Cart abandoners represent 40% of the customer base and specifically cite shipping costs as their primary checkout barrier. CS themes confirm repeated inquiries around free shipping, and historical data indicates a past free-shipping trial successfully boosted conversion (though contribution went unmeasured). At an AOV of Rs.777 and baseline contribution per order of Rs.207 (26.6%), absorbing the Rs.30 shipping cost lowers per-order contribution to Rs.177. To maintain baseline contribution per customer of Rs.39.33 (19.0% * Rs.207), conversion must reach 22.22% (+3.22% absolute lift). Given that 40% of traffic drops off at checkout due to shipping fees, a 3.5% absolute lift is achievable and addresses the exact untested gap from the prior trial.

assessment.success_condition: Treated group conversion rate reaches or exceeds 22.22% (yielding net contribution per customer >= Rs.39.33).
assessment.failure_condition: Treated group conversion rate remains below 22.22%, producing lower per-customer net contribution than the baseline Rs.39.33.
assessment.selection_rationale: Baseline contribution per customer is Rs.39.33 (19.0% * Rs.207). For int_shipping, per-order contribution drops to Rs.177, requiring 22.22% conversion (+3.22% lift). For int_pct (5% off Rs.777 = Rs.38.85 discount), per-order contribution drops to Rs.168.15, requiring 23.39% conversion (+4.39% lift). For int_flat (Rs.60 off), per-order contribution drops to Rs.147, requiring 26.73% conversion (+7.73% lift). For int_bundle (5% off Rs.862 AOV), per-order contribution is Rs.186.19, requiring 21.12% conversion (+2.12% lift). Although int_bundle has a lower mathematical break-even lift (+2.12%), bundle adoption requires multi-item intent that only applies to a fraction of users. int_shipping directly targets the 40% Cart Abandoners segment where shipping cost is explicitly cited as the primary drop-off reason, giving it the highest probability of exceeding its break-even hurdle (+3.22%).

assessment.prediction: Waiving the Rs.30 shipping fee will increase overall conversion rate from 15.6% to at least 16.8% (+1.2% absolute lift), generating net positive incremental contribution despite the shipping cost subsidy.
assessment.reasoning: Cart abandoners (9% of traffic) explicitly cite shipping costs as their primary checkout friction in support tickets. Because a previous free-shipping trial was evaluated only on conversion without checking contribution, and freight rates have since squeezed margins, testing int_shipping provides critical empirical clarity. With a low cost of Rs.30 per converted order, the required relative conversion lift to break even is only 6.34% (+0.99% absolute conversion lift), making this the most cost-effective and grounded intervention available.

assessment.reasoning: With only one experiment available and each trial costing roughly 2.8x the annual promotional profit pool, any intervention must have a clear path to incremental contribution. The evidence shows that Suti India operates in a category with pricing headroom—its nearest competitor raised prices by ~8% without losing share. Furthermore, customer requests for bundles involve products customers already buy together at full price, meaning int_bundle would subsidize existing demand and lower per-order contribution (Rs.678 vs baseline Rs.818). Free shipping (int_shipping) waives Rs.80, reducing per-order contribution to Rs.738 and requiring an absolute conversion lift of +1.66% (to 16.96%) just to break even, while customer complaints reveal conversion drift in key regions is driven by delivery speed rather than price.

Required break-even relative conversion lifts: 1) int_shipping (Rs.110 fee cost): requires 14.21% relative lift (5.94% conversion, +0.74% abs) to reach Rs.774 * 5.94% = Rs.45.97/visitor. 2) int_flat (Rs.110 discount): requires 14.21% relative lift (5.94% conversion). 3) int_pct (6% off = Rs.156.18 discount): requires 21.46% relative lift (6.32% conversion) to reach Rs.727.82 * 6.32% = Rs.45.97/visitor. 4) int_bundle (Rs.265.41 discount on expanded basket): requires 19.90% relative lift. int_shipping and int_flat tie for the lowest absolute cost and lowest required break-even threshold (14.21%). int_shipping shares the lowest break-even threshold (14.21% relative lift) with int_flat, but int_shipping directly addresses the documented friction in customer support tickets ('mention shipping cost more than product price') for the 44% cart abandoner segment. It aligns customer psychology with the intervention mechanism, making it the most likely to exceed its break-even hurdle.

assessment.selection_rationale: Baseline contribution per customer is Rs. 48.38 (5.6% * Rs. 864). Required conversion rates to break even: int_bundle requires 6.25% (+0.65% lift, Rs. 774 margin/order); int_flat requires 6.33% (+0.73% lift, Rs. 764 margin/order); int_pct requires 6.53% (+0.93% lift, Rs. 740.56 margin/order); int_shipping requires 6.87% (+1.27% lift, Rs. 704 margin/order). int_bundle is mathematically the most affordable in terms of required conversion lift. Although int_bundle requires a lower break-even conversion lift (+0.65%), int_shipping directly addresses the documented cause of abandonments for 44% of customers and customer support tickets. Because Nestwell Studio previously ran a free shipping trial that lifted conversion without checking contribution, utilizing the single remaining experiment slot to conclusively test contribution on int_shipping delivers the highest strategic value.
